facts.fact: The ANEC director-general's presentation of August 2025 states 383 civil-status centres installed, with network equipment put in on site by the state company SENUM SA, and 235 centres in service, connected to the network and operational, of 400 centres to be interconnected; the document gives no date for the counts and its own date is used.

Agents and officers at the civil-status centres, which the communes run, register and issue acts in the management software of the national civil-status register (RNEC), hosted at three national sites: 112,881 declarations were registered through the RNEC in 2024 and 108,233 from 1 January to 3 July 2025, on ANEC's figures.

ANEC counts 235 civil-status centres in service, connected to the network and operational, against 383 installed and 400 to be interconnected, in its presentation of August 2025; the count is of civil-status centres, not of communes, and no total of communes is given. The document gives no date for the counts and its own date is used.

The civil-status information system and the interconnection of the centres are run by the Agence nationale de l'état civil, under the ministry of urbanism, local authorities and territorial planning, with the state company SENUM SA installing the network equipment, as stated in August 2025.

ANEC's presentation of August 2025 sets the full digitalisation of all civil-status centres as its perspective, cites Vision Sénégal 2050 as naming the digitalisation of local authorities' services, and names a national civil-status strategy and a second phase, NEKKAL 2, both still to be financed.

ANEC's presentation of August 2025 names no funder or budget line for the centres' interconnection; it lists financing of the national civil-status strategy and of NEKKAL 2, and strengthening ANEC's own financial means, as things still to be obtained.
